## What to do

Adapt the upstream compaction doc (tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md, 394 lines) for our Elixir system.

## Upstream source

- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/branch-summarization.ts
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts

## Output

Create docs/compaction.md

## How to adapt

1. **Overview section**: Keep the comparison table (Compaction vs Branch Summarization) — it is technology-agnostic and can be preserved as-is.

2. **When It Triggers**: The formula `contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens` is preserved. Update the config path from `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` to `~/.octo_pi/settings.json`. Note our `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction` module.

3. **How It Works**: Replace the ASCII diagram with our Elixir terminology. The cut point algorithm is the same (walk backwards accumulating tokens until keepRecentTokens reached). Reference our modules:
   - `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction.find_cut_point/2` instead of TypeScript findCutPoint
   - `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction.generate_summary/3` instead of TypeScript compact()
   - `OctoPi.Coder.SessionEntry.Compaction` instead of CompactionEntry TypeScript interface
   - `OctoPi.Coder.SessionEntry.BranchSummary` instead of BranchSummaryEntry

4. **Split Turns**: The concept is the same. Update the ASCII diagram labels to reference our field names. Note that our `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction.CutPoint` module handles this.

5. **Cut Point Rules**: Identical rules — user messages, assistant messages, BashExecution, custom messages. Never cut at tool results. This is algorithm-level, not language-level.

6. **CompactionEntry Structure**: Convert the TypeScript interface to Elixir struct definition. Show our `OctoPi.Coder.SessionEntry.Compaction` struct:
   ```elixir
   defstruct type: :compaction, id: nil, parent_id: nil, timestamp: nil,
             summary: "", first_kept_entry_id: nil, tokens_before: 0, details: %{}
   ```
   Note: `from_hook` field is dropped (legacy TypeScript field name).

7. **Branch Summarization**: Same structure — convert BranchSummaryEntry to our `OctoPi.Coder.SessionEntry.BranchSummary` struct.

8. **Summary Format**: The markdown template is identical. Preserve verbatim.

9. **Custom Summarization via Extensions**: This section needs the most work:
   - Replace all TypeScript `pi.on()` / `pi.registerProvider()` calls with our Elixir extension API
   - Show our event system: `OctoPi.Coder.Extension.on(event, handler)` pattern
   - Replace `serializeConversation()` with our `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction.serialize_conversation/1`
   - Replace `convertToLlm()` with our message conversion
   - Show how `session_before_compact` and `session_before_tree` events work in our system

10. **Settings**: Update path to `~/.octo_pi/settings.json`. Keep the JSON schema identical (our SettingsManager mirrors upstream).

## What to preserve verbatim

- The compaction ASCII diagram concept (redraw with Elixir field names)
- The summary format template (markdown)
- The settings JSON schema
- The cut point rules
- The comparison table (Compaction vs Branch Summarization)

## What to note as divergent

- Check if our `OctoPi.Coder.Compaction` implementation differs in any algorithm (token counting, cut point selection, iterative summarization). Document any differences.
- Check if our extension hook API differs from the TypeScript `pi.on()` pattern.

## Key upstream references to include

- [compaction.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts)
- [branch-summarization.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/branch-summarization.ts)
- [utils.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts)
- [session-manager.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts)

## Testing the doc

After writing, verify:
1. All code references point to our actual modules (grep for them to confirm they exist)
2. The summary format template is complete
3. Settings table matches our actual defaults
4. Extension hooks section accurately reflects our Extension API
